prompt: Prime-time adult animated sitcom characters with simple rounded cartoon bodies, flat colour and black outlines, but every face is painted with startling real skin: pores, stubble, wrinkles, wet tired eyes, real eyelids, far more lifelike than anything around it, no feature exaggerated. Every colour is laid on in thick visible oil brushstrokes. Night in a secret 1930s basement, close and side-on on a tall skinny mayor in a bowler hat with a gold chain, a long narrow face, hollow cheeks and a pencil-thin grey moustache, his shirt-sleeves rolled up, waistcoat, sweat running down his face, his real-skinned face large in frame and off-centre left, teeth gritted in a grin, heaving a coal shovel into the open firebox of a huge black iron printing press with a simple face painted on its side and a coal firebox in its belly glowing red hot. The firebox blazes red-orange at the right edge of frame and lights his face from below; sheets of blank green paper money with no printing on them fly past his head; flour dust drifts down onto his bowler from the wooden ceiling. A cool emerald lamp glows far behind him. Most of the frame in deep shadow; the brightest values are the fire on his face and the flying notes. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
